flashcard_questions.a: A set showing several different locations on stage at the same time.

flashcard_questions.q: Why would a box set not work for Blood Brothers?
flashcard_questions.a: A box set shows only one location, and the action moves between many places.

flashcard_questions.q: Which household would sit stage right to reinforce privilege and comfort?
In traditional staging, stage right suggests positive experiences and stage left suggests ____ ones.
flashcard_questions.a: Negative experiences, which is why the Johnstone household sits stage left.
A wheeled platform that rolls scenery on and off stage.

flashcard_questions.q: What is a gobo in lighting design?
flashcard_questions.a: A disc placed inside a spotlight to project a pattern.

flashcard_questions.q: Which gobo shows that Mickey is imprisoned?
flashcard_questions.a: A prison bar gobo, projected with white light.

flashcard_questions.q: Which gobo creates the Town Hall for the final confrontation?
Which staging type was used for the original production of Blood Brothers?
How many staging types must you know for the written exam?
What is the apron of a stage?
flashcard_questions.a: The area at the front that sticks out in front of the proscenium arch.

flashcard_questions.q: Why does an actor step onto the apron for an intimate moment?
flashcard_questions.a: It breaks the fourth wall and brings the audience closer.

flashcard_questions.q: Where does the audience sit in traverse staging?
flashcard_questions.a: On two opposite sides, with the stage in between.

flashcard_questions.q: Why is promenade staging impractical for Blood Brothers?
flashcard_questions.a: Audience members with physical difficulties could not move between locations.

flashcard_questions.q: What advantage does a fly loft give a set designer?
flashcard_questions.a: Scenery can be stored above the stage and lowered when needed.
